poster_title: INSIDE: LLMS’ INTERNAL STATES RETAIN THE POWER OF HALLUCINATION DETECTION
authors: Chao Chen, Kai Liu, Ze Chen, Yi Gu, Yue Wu, Mingyuan Tao, Zhihang Fu, Jieping Ye
paper_info: Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024

content: LLMs often produce factually incorrect or nonsensical outputs, known as knowledge hallucination.
Previous methods focused on logit-level uncertainty or language-level self-consistency, losing semantic information.
INSIDE framework addresses these limitations by leveraging internal states for hallucination detection.
Proposed a generalized INSIDE framework for hallucination detection using LLMs' internal states.

content: Conducted experiments on popular LLMs and QA benchmarks.
Performed ablation studies to validate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

content: INSIDE framework achieved state-of-the-art performance in hallucination detection on multiple QA benchmarks.

content: INSIDE framework and EigenScore metric provide a novel and effective way to detect hallucinations in LLMs.
Feature clipping approach helps reduce overconfident hallucinations, improving LLM reliability.
